stem: What ultrasound finding is characteristic of an intussusception?

options.text: Multiple concentric rings in the upper abdomen
A double bubble of fluid-filled structures
A pyloric channel length exceeding 14 mm
Branching lucency within the portal venous system
Free intraperitoneal air under the diaphragm

explanation: The target or donut sign is the characteristic ultrasound finding in intussusception.
rationale: It occurs when one segment of bowel telescopes into another, producing concentric rings on transverse ultrasound.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because intussusception classically appears as a target or donut sign with concentric rings on ultrasound.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a double bubble is a sign of duodenal atresia, not intussusception.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because an elongated pyloric channel suggests pyloric stenosis, not intussusception.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because branching lucency in the portal venous system indicates portal venous gas, not intussusception.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because free intraperitoneal air suggests bowel perforation, not intussusception.

source.hint: This sign is created by one segment of bowel telescoping into another.
